report.verdict: An office administrator at a dental group, with retail management before that, but no descriptions of the work.
write_up: Office administrator at a dental group, with retail management before that. This is a common profile: a headline that repeats the current job, no About, and titles with nothing under them. A recruiter has to guess what you did and is likely to move on.

The move from Sales Associate to Assistant Store Manager at Brightway is worth keeping visible. It shows progression, but neither job says what you did, so there isn't a description to use as a model yet.
Start with the Harlow job, then add an About and sharpen the headline. Put your actual dental office work in those places so someone hiring an office administrator can see what you've handled.

cards.line: Office Administrator at Harlow Dental Group
cards.cannot_tell: This repeats your current job without saying what you handle there. Add your specialty beside the dental group so a recruiter can tell what kind of office work you do.
cards.example: Office Administrator | Harlow Dental Group | [your specialty]
cards.question: What kind of office work is most central to your job at Harlow?

cards.cannot_tell: There's no introduction to your work at Harlow or the experience you brought from Brightway. Start with what you do and who you support.
cards.example: I work as an Office Administrator at Harlow Dental Group. I [what you do] for [who you support].
cards.question: What do you handle at Harlow, and who do you support?

cards.line: The Office Administrator job at Harlow Dental Group has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: Your current job leaves the actual work blank. A search for scheduling, billing or insurance verification has no words from this description to match. Add the work you do, not every possible office duty.
cards.example: [What you run: the schedule, billing or the front desk] for [who you support] at Harlow Dental Group.
cards.question: At Harlow, do you handle scheduling, billing or the front desk? Who do you support, and how much of that work is yours?

cards.where: Brightway Home Goods, Assistant Store Manager
cards.line: The Assistant Store Manager job at Brightway Home Goods has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: The title shows a step up at Brightway, but not what you managed. Staffing, opening and closing, or the cash office would give a recruiter a way to understand the job if those were yours.
cards.example: [Your work: staffing, opening and closing, or the cash office] at Brightway Home Goods, with [number of people per shift].
cards.question: As Assistant Store Manager, did you handle staffing, opening and closing, or the cash office? How many people were on a shift?

cards.cannot_tell: Teamwork doesn't name the work your office job turns on. The three skills shown don't yet tell a recruiter which office systems or processes you use.
cards.example: [the scheduling or billing software you use] | [insurance verification, if you do it] | [another skill from your office work]
cards.question: Which software, office processes and other daily skills do you use at Harlow?

fit.why: Your headline and current title name Office Administrator, with Assistant Store Manager as your prior job.
fit.level: mid-level, Office Administrator is your current title
fit.note: 'Office Administrator' is in your headline and current title. 'Dental Group' is in your headline and employer name. 'Microsoft Office' and 'Teamwork' are in your top skills. Someone hiring for this job may also search for scheduling, billing and insurance verification, none of which appears on your profile. If they describe your work, put the relevant specialty in your headline and the tasks in your Harlow description; use your About to connect that work to your earlier experience. Start by naming your main office specialty in the headline.
